scope: Offline synthetic receiver-side erasure of already planned frames. No operational link access.
question: Which representation detects a genuinely failed OFF transition by the original six-hour deadline under frame erasure?
episode_seed: 41000000 + 100000 * profile_index + index; indices 0 to 159 inclusive. Even healthy, odd late failure. No prior test seeds reused.
design: 480 independent generated episodes, 80 healthy and 80 late-failure per profile. Every episode is reused across all 36 conditions. Base physical settings and frozen detector. Three OFF targets per episode; fault-episode status alone never labels earlier successful OFFs as failures.
loss_opportunity: Each scheduled contact has an independent pseudorandom one-third eligibility gate shared across arms, methods and rates within an episode and schedule. At an eligible nonempty contact erase at most one frame; empty batches produce no erasure. This is not a one-third per-frame loss probability.
erasure_rule: Uniform: one frame from the planned batch. Selective: choose among frames carrying an explicit observed OFF context record, otherwise use the same uniform choice. Common random frame priorities break ties; matching singleton or unmarked batches give identical losses. Mask sees planned batch metadata only, no fault truth, sensor values, future telemetry or ground decision; assumes access to event-type metadata at a trusted application boundary.
fairness: Identical gates and one-frame cap do not imply equal erased bytes or counts across policies. Report actual denominators, counts, bytes and fraction of transmissions lost. No initial full-channel outage, independent ACK loss, spoofing or receiver compromise.
feedback: Common serialized planning, fixed ACK slot on attempted frames, no ACK for an erased frame; charge transmitted bytes and occupied slots separately. No within-contact repacking; later contacts use the acknowledged cache so undelivered observations remain eligible under the frozen policy.
primary: KazSTSAT calculated contacts at 32 bit/s. For each faulty episode, fraction of true failed OFFs with an actual correct fault decision by 21600 s, then average within profile and equal weight across three profiles. Later corrections do not undo issued wrong decisions; nondetections stay in denominator. A matched lossless arm contextualizes degradation.
inference: Six primary paired method contrasts: all three pairwise differences in each of the two erasure conditions. Resample fault-bearing episodes jointly across conditions within profile. 20000 bootstrap draws, seed 8317402, two-sided percentile limits with alpha 0.05/6 per contrast; approximate simultaneous family inference. Endpoints exactly constant in sample do not imply population certainty. A higher rate with inconclusive interval is an observed lead only. No new equivalence declaration.
secondary: 8 bit/s and periodic controls; descriptive profile and per-schedule/per-rate statistics. Registered practical metrics include healthy false alarms, wrong nominal on truly faulty OFFs, no decision, average six-hour-capped delay, actual bytes, occupied airtime, contact and cost through diagnosis/censoring. Report actual conditional counts and six-hour costs for unresolved cases separately. For matched selective minus random and loss minus lossless comparisons report uncertainty as descriptive.
verification: Development smoke uses separate old development seeds; check delivery and deadline parity with original simulator on lossless development cases, causal erasures, feedback and byte accounting, exact denominators, paired inference and completeness. Scientific source changes after the freeze require a documented correction and rerun of the affected work.
manuscript: A separate editable conference copy and a 10-12-page PDF inclusive of references. The 6000-episode baseline and this 480-episode extension have separate designs and results.
interpretation: Results conditional on specified synthetic erasure model and link allocations. No attribution of a loss pattern to a real adversary and no mission fault-security validation.
